summary: The technician's clean-probe measurement of 2.1 Ω on the 5V rail with normal 4.2 kΩ on the 3.3V rail establishes a hard short localized to the 5V net, consistent with global rail collapse on both USB and DC inputs.
evidenceSynthesis: The technician-reported ev-bench-101 supersedes the unstable ev-bench-100 and directly demonstrates a 5V-to-GND hard short while the 3.3V net remains healthy. This strengthens a primary 5V rail overload and contradicts a 3.3V-regulator-induced drag-down. Regulator-internal versus downstream-load location of the 5V short remains unverified without isolation testing.

revisedHypotheses.title: Dead short on 5V rail overloading F1 polyfuse and NCP1117 regulator
revisedHypotheses.explanationOfChange: The technician measured a stable 2.1 Ω 5V-to-GND short in ev-bench-101, directly aligning with a hard 5V rail overload dragging both supplies into current-limit.

revisedHypotheses.title: Shorted LP2985-33 3.3V regulator or 3.3V rail short dragging 5V down
revisedHypotheses.explanationOfChange: The technician measured 4.2 kΩ on the 3.3V rail to GND in ev-bench-101, which is normal and conflicts with a shorted 3.3V regulator/rail as the cause of 5V collapse.

revisedHypotheses.title: Failed NCP1117ST50T3G 5V regulator internally shorted or D1/F1 degraded after overvoltage/reverse event
revisedHypotheses.explanationOfChange: No D1/F1 or NCP1117 VIN/VOUT isolation measurements have been reported, so whether the 2.1 Ω short is internal to the regulator or in a downstream 5V load cannot yet be distinguished.
revisedHypotheses.suggestedVerification: Technician to perform unpowered diode-mode on D1 and resistance on F1 and NCP1117 VIN/VOUT to GND, then isolate NCP1117 VOUT from 5V rail and re-measure 5V resistance to localize short.

nextRecommendedChecks.title: Isolate NCP1117 5V regulator output to localize short
nextRecommendedChecks.procedure: With board unpowered, lift or desolder NCP1117 VOUT pin from 5V net. Re-measure 5V rail to GND and regulator VOUT pad to GND separately.
nextRecommendedChecks.expectedResult: If 5V rail remains ~2 Ω with regulator isolated, short is downstream; if rail recovers to >1 kΩ and regulator pad is ~2 Ω, regulator is internally shorted.
safetyNotes: Keep board unpowered during desoldering and resistance checks to prevent thermal stress

nextRecommendedChecks.title: Systematic downstream 5V load isolation
toolsNeeded: Thermal camera or low-voltage current injection supply (optional)
nextRecommendedChecks.procedure: With regulator isolated, measure resistance of downstream 5V branches (C1/C2, ATmega16U2 VCC, ATmega328P VCC). Remove or lift suspect caps/ICs one at a time and re-check 5V resistance.
nextRecommendedChecks.expectedResult: Resistance should rise from 2.1 Ω to >1 kΩ when shorted component is removed; healthy branches measure kΩ range.
safetyNotes: Do not reapply USB/DC power until 5V short is cleared; use only unpowered resistance or <1V current-limited injection if needed

safetyWarnings: Do not power the board via USB or DC barrel jack while the technician-reported 2.1 Ω 5V short persists — risk of regulator overheating, polyfuse damage, and PCB thermal runaway.
Perform all further checks unpowered with cold resistance/continuity methods before any energized voltage measurements.
limitations: Regulator-internal versus downstream-load location of the 5V short not yet distinguished — requires NCP1117 isolation measurement.
No downstream IC or capacitor-level isolation data yet; exact shorted component on 5V net remains unidentified.
